title: Locate the Event and a Reported Cause
definition: Permission not to pay a certain tax or perform a required duty.
content:
Our case starts at Cavite on 20 January 1872. A mutiny is a military uprising against authority. Fort San Felipe and the nearby naval arsenal belonged to this setting. An arsenal is a place supplying military equipment and work.

Why were people unhappy? French writer Edmond Plauchut, writing in 1877, connected the uprising with workers losing exemptions from tax and required labor. He described privileges connected with their retirement. An exemption means a person does not have to pay a certain tax or perform a duty. Removing it can change what that person owes. This is a reported cause in his account, not a statement from every worker.

Imagine a classroom example: a rule changes what a person is required to pay. Understanding that change helps explain a complaint. It does not tell us everyone had the same goal. Our next source comparison asks whether the accounts agree about how widely the uprising was planned. Keep Cavite separate from the later execution at Bagumbayan in Manila.
clues: 20 January 1872: a military uprising in Cavite, at Fort San Felipe.
Plauchut's 1877 account connects the uprising with the loss of tax and required-labor exemptions, including retirement privileges.
An exemption removes a duty for someone. Losing it can create a grievance, or complaint.
task: What does the reported loss of an exemption mean?
Workers would lose permission not to pay a tax or perform a required duty.
Every worker received a new payment from the government.
The arsenal became a school open to everyone.
An accusation automatically became proof of mutiny leadership.
reason: Plauchut connected the uprising with lost exemptions: a change in what workers owed. This explains a reported grievance, not every participant's goal.

title: Compare Two Accounts, Then Check the Claim
definition: A description or explanation of the past made by a person or group.
content:
Read two modern summaries of historical accounts. These are our paraphrases, not quotations.

Account A: Edmond Plauchut wrote in 1877. He linked the uprising with lost tax and required-labor exemptions. He also described mutineers expecting support that did not arrive. A worker complaint and an expectation of support can both appear in an account. Calling his account only a complaint with no plans would leave out that detail.

Account B: Governor Rafael de Izquierdo reported on 31 January 1872. He described the suppression as stopping plans prepared in advance against Spanish rule. This tells us how a colonial official presented the event, not that every accusation in his report is automatically true.

Compare the emphasis: a reported grievance and failed support in A; organized plans in B. A cause is why someone may act. The extent asks how widely action was planned or supported. These are different questions. A wider plan does not by itself prove that Gomes, Burgos and Zamora organized it. Authorities accused the priests, but keep the accusation separate from proof.

Connect the source cards and explain what they support. We do not label either summary the opinion of every French, Spanish or Filipino person.
clues: His account links lost exemptions with the uprising and describes expected support that did not arrive.
His official report presents the suppression as stopping plans prepared in advance against Spanish rule.
An account of a grievance or a wider plan does not by itself prove that the priests organized the event.
task: Which comparison fits the two source summaries?
Plauchut discusses lost exemptions and failed support; Izquierdo stresses plans prepared in advance.
Plauchut says no one expected support anywhere.
Izquierdo says the event was only a change in retirement benefits.
Both summaries prove every accused person organized the uprising.
reason: Plauchut emphasizes lost exemptions and describes failed support; Izquierdo stresses advance planning. Compare the emphasis without turning an accusation into proof.

effects.label: Plauchut: lost exemptions and support that did not arrive.
Izquierdo: plans prepared in advance against Spanish rule.
Limit: these summaries alone do not prove that the priests organized the event.

pairs.label: Plauchut, 1877
pairs.action: A later published account discusses changed duties and hoped-for support.
pairs.feedback: His account includes a reported grievance and an expectation of support, not just one of those ideas.

pairs.label: Izquierdo, January 1872
pairs.action: An official report describes stopping plans prepared beforehand.
pairs.feedback: This is the official report's interpretation, which still needs examination.

pairs.label: Our comparison rule
pairs.action: Ask what the accounts show before making a claim about who organized the uprising.
pairs.feedback: A cause, a plan and proof about a named person are different questions.

title: Explain Causes, Claims and Responses
definition: An account connecting causes, events and responses while showing what evidence supports.
content:
Your case now connects a reported cause, an event, a claim and a later response. Plauchut links the uprising with lost exemptions and describes support that did not arrive. Izquierdo presents plans prepared in advance. Their different emphases do not settle who organized the event merely by naming an accused person.

Locate the Cavite Mutiny on 20 January 1872. Explain that authorities accused Gomes, Burgos and Zamora, and that the priests were executed at Bagumbayan on 17 February. Then identify later remembrance, such as Rizal's dedication. Punishment does not turn an accusation into proof.

Try this report frame: "According to ___, a cause or plan was ___. The other account emphasizes ___. The January event was followed by ___. A later response was ___. Our cards do not prove ___." Use the source names rather than saying all people held one view. Review a difficult topic before targeted practice.
clues: Explain both the reported loss of exemptions and the question of planned or expected support.
January mutiny, February execution, later remembrance.
Comparing accounts does not turn an accusation into proof.
task: Which report connects the case evidence?
A January mutiny was followed by accusations and a February execution; later remembrance expressed concern about injustice.
A novel dedication was the mutiny and happened before January 1872.
All reform supporters certainly organized the uprising.
One memorial tells us every detail of the trial and every person's view.
reason: Connect a reported cause, competing emphases about plans, the event sequence and later remembrance without treating an accusation as proof.
